quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink affect your riding?

options.text: Yes, it can affect your judgment and ability to ride safely.
No, one drink usually has no effect on the body.
Yes, but the effect only lasts a short time.
Yes, but you can eliminate it by drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can affect your judgment and ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding skills. Your body must have time to get rid of the alcohol. Drinking coffee will not help.

questions.question: How important are turn signals on a motorcycle?

options.text: More important than on cars and trucks.
Only important when another vehicle is right next to you.
Less important than on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: More important than on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more at risk than car and truck drivers. Using signals is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before each ride.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.

questions.question: How does a passenger affect motorcycle handling?

options.text: Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can change how the motorcycle handles.
Helps new riders learn different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Why is proper clothing important when riding?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Your arms and legs should not be fully covered.
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather.
It can protect you in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly but allow you to move freely.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.correctAnswerText: By downshifting.
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a way to slow down. Be aware that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. Take breaks at least every two hours on long trips to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: What is the best way to survive a motorcycle crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is properly fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is properly fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is properly fastened is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: How can you make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Ride with a large flag on the frame.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on at all times. Wear bright, reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and brake lights properly.

questions.question: What type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing so other drivers can see you. Bright, reflective gear makes it easier for people to spot you on the road.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should always look ahead for:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to stay alert to traffic, road hazards, and escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to changes.

questions.question: You should check your mirrors:

options.text: As part of your normal checking routine.
As little as possible because they distract you.
Rarely, because other drivers can see you easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your normal checking routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. Regular mirror checks should be part of your normal routine.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars are dangerous. A driver may pull out without looking. Doors may open into your lane, and people may step out from between cars.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Turns the same way as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used in curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar handles turns differently than a regular two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can go over the speed limit until the pass is done.
You can ignore "No passing" markings if you started in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal zones.
questions.explanation: Only pass when it is safe and legal. Always stay within the speed limit while passing.

questions.question: A plastic face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need regular checks?
questions.correctAnswerText: The paint
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, chain, fasteners, and brakes. Small problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous in traffic.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane behind a car:

options.text: You are in the best spot to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more than their side mirror.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not your whole face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Do not protect your eyes as well as eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your whole face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Regular eyeglasses are not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When you see an object or uneven surface you cannot avoid, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stand slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stand slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright. Stand slightly off the seat so your knees can absorb some of the impact force. Just before hitting it, give the throttle a slight twist to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What is one benefit of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always try to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Compared to large groups, small groups are easier for other vehicles to pass safely. They are less likely to get separated by traffic or traffic lights. They also require less pressure on slower riders to speed up and catch the group.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when you ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that protects you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. The best choices are a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: What can reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash.
